## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

```{r Workshop 2 Start}
#--------------------------------------------------#
# MB5370: Visualisation - turning data into graphics
# Natalie Wasinski
# May 21 2026
# Workspace: D:/MB5370_Techniques_1/Module_1/Workshop2.Rmd
#----------------------------------------------------------#

library(tidyverse) #remind R it has package, don't have to reinstall every time
mpg #look at data

ggplot(data = mpg) + geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))
# Plot displaying engine on x and fuel efficiency on y
```

```{r Graphing Template}
# Graphing template
ggplot(data = <DATA>) + <GEOM_FUNCTION>(mapping = eas(<MAPPINGS>))

# Graphing Aesthetics
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = class))
```
```{r size class graph}
# Change point size by class
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, size = class))
```
```{r transparency graph}
# Change point transparency by class (alpha)
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, alpha = class))
```
```{r Graph point shape by class}
# Changing plot points on the graph to be shapes according to class
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, shape = class))
```
```{r Manual Graph Aesthetic}
# Set properties manually, such as offering a number or a colour
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), color = "blue")

# other manual appearance alterations include the name of a color as a character string, the size of a point in mm, the shape of a point as a number
```
```{r}
# testing out mapping an aesthetic to something other than a variable name
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), color = displ < 5)
# says object 'displ' not found
```

```{r Facet and Panel plots}
# Use facet_wrap() function to split up data into sub plots  using a single variable - only use discrete variables
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) + 
  facet_wrap(~ class)
```
```{r 2 varaible facet}
# to split up graphs using more than one variable, split them using ~
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) + 
  facet_grid(drv ~ cyl)
```
```{r}
# use a . if you do not want to facet in the rows or column dimension
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) + 
  facet_grid(. ~ cyl)
```
```{r Exercise}
?facet_grid
#Exercise 2.20
#nrow and ncol: set of variables or expressions quoted by vars(), defining faceting grounds on rows or columns dimension - usage: NULL
#control layout of individual panels: scales, labels, space, margins, axes
```

```{r Fitting simple lines}
# To display data as points, use geom_point()
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))

# To display same data as a smooth line fit through the points, use geom_smooth()
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))

# geom is what represents the data, change the geom function to change geom type (or how the data is represented)

# can change line type using a variable to control it
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, linetype = drv))
# separates the cars into three different line types based on drv (front wheel, rear wheel, or 4wd)

# Use group argument to show that our data is in fact grouped
ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, group = drv))

# Change the color of each line based on drv value
ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = drv),
    show.legend = FALSE)

# Plot multiple geoms on the single plot - add commands together
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))

# To specify different data for each layer use the "subcompact" to select a subset of the data and plot only that subset
install.packages("ggplot2")
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(color = class)) + 
  geom_smooth(data = filter(mpg, class = "subcompact")),(se = FALSE)

# FINISH END OF 2.21
```
